page: Amazon Web Services c4.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.9 GHz. It is equipped with 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding 1.88 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates on the Xen hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the c4.4xlarge in the average tier across most workloads. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1182.0 and a multi-core score of 7354.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 15674.33. Memory bandwidth tests show 851.49 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 89.52 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For specialized workloads, it handles Redis SET operations at 6.16 million operations per second and delivers 11.52 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. Large language model inference speeds are moderate for a small 135M model, but drop to a weak 23.37 tokens per second for prompt processing on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4.4xlarge offers a dedicated compute profile without the added expense of bundled local storage or GPU hardware, making it a resource-dense option for CPU-bound tasks. The lack of local NVMe storage requires external storage attachments for persistent data. This instance is best suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, web serving, data decompression, and moderate database operations.
